what_its_for: Fluocinonide is a strong steroid cream, gel, ointment, or solution applied to the skin. It helps reduce redness, swelling, itching, and irritation caused by certain skin conditions such as eczema, psoriasis, allergic reactions, and rashes.
how_to_take: Wash your hands before and after applying this medicine. Clean and dry the affected skin area. Apply a thin layer of fluocinonide directly to the affected skin and gently rub it in. Do not cover the area with a bandage or wrap unless your doctor tells you to. Do not apply to your face, groin, or underarms unless specifically directed by your doctor. Avoid getting this medicine in your eyes, mouth, or nose. Do not swallow it.
dosing: Use fluocinonide exactly as your doctor prescribes. It is usually applied 2 to 4 times per day, depending on the form and strength your doctor prescribed. The 0.1% cream (Vanos) is typically applied once or twice daily. Do not use more than prescribed, and do not use it for longer than your doctor recommends. Typically, treatment should not last longer than 2 weeks unless your doctor instructs otherwise.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store fluocinonide at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Keep the tube or container tightly closed when not in use. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Do not use fluocinonide on areas of broken, infected, or very thin skin unless directed by your doctor. Avoid using it near your eyes, as it can cause increased eye pressure or cataracts. Do not use on the face, armpits, or groin without your doctor's approval. Avoid wrapping the treated area tightly with bandages or plastic wrap unless told to do so by your doctor. Do not use more than prescribed or for longer than recommended, as this can cause serious side effects. Avoid using other skin products or medications on the same area without checking with your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor if you notice any of the following: your skin condition is not improving or is getting worse after 2 weeks of treatment; signs of skin infection such as increased redness, warmth, swelling, pus, or pain; skin thinning, stretch marks, or discoloration where you applied the cream; unusual weight gain, swelling, or puffiness in your face; extreme tiredness or weakness; easy bruising; vision changes; or if you accidentally get the medicine in your eyes. Seek emergency care if you have signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, hives, difficulty breathing, or swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat.
when_it_works: You may start to notice improvement in your symptoms such as reduced itching and redness within a few days of starting treatment. Full improvement may take 1 to 2 weeks. If your symptoms do not improve after 2 weeks, contact your doctor. Do not use this medicine for longer than prescribed, even if your symptoms improve.
special_populations: Children: Fluocinonide should be used with extra caution in children because their skin absorbs more of the medicine, which increases the risk of serious side effects such as growth problems and hormonal changes. Use the smallest effective amount for the shortest time possible. Avoid using tight diapers or plastic pants on infants being treated in the diaper area. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before using this medicine. Fluocinonide should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. If breastfeeding, do not apply the medicine to your breasts or nipples. Elderly patients: Older adults may have thinner skin and may be more sensitive to side effects. Use as directed by your doctor.
